Express null branches explicitly so SQL NULL cannot make an invalid check pass.” “Effective completed state requires a completion reference/origin: current `status=completed`, or current `status=archived` and `archived_from_status=completed`.” “Suspension reference is required for current suspended, archived-with-origin-suspended, and effective-completed-with-completion-origin-suspended.” “Outside those effective states, retained historical references are allowed. Do not require a suspension reference just because `archived_from_status` retains suspended while current status is active/draft/etc.” “All references have real audit FK integrity. Same-project, expected semantic type, allowed original transition, source version and completion-to-suspension association are application validations under the root lock, not cross-table SQL CHECKs.” “Existing create/template/import paths remain draft and do not copy event references, origin or receipts. nodes.label: Consistency boundary
nodes.rationale: Run executes the persisted state under an atomic case-row lock/reload, deriving calculation and frozen snapshot from that same state. PATCH then POST are separate requests; another editor may save between them. Returned `input_snapshot` is authoritative. The UI must render results against that snapshot and serialize its own same-case saves/runs. No guarantee of cross-client optimistic revision matching is introduced.

nodes.label: Existing DecisionCase
nodes.rationale: No new entity or column. Retain project ownership, title, selected methods, ordered criteria and all existing method inputs. `dematel_matrix` is existing editable JSON containing row-major directed judgments in criteria order. - Empty/uninitialized draft: `[]`; rendered initialization supplies zero diagonal and null off-diagonal values.

nodes.label: Existing DecisionRun
nodes.rationale: No new entity or migration. Retain foreign keys `case`, `project`, `extracted_by`, method `dematel`, immutable `input_snapshot`, immutable `result`, and `extracted_at`. Snapshot uses the existing deep-copy helper, preserving title, ordered criteria, selected methods, direct influences and existing method inputs. Calculation and snapshot must come from one locked authoritative case state. The result records normalized/total matrices, normalization factor, ordered criterion results and the versioned numerical policy described in the result contract.

nodes.label: Migration decision

nodes.label: Consistency boundary
nodes.rationale: An ISM-only atomic path reloads/locks the active case by project and case ID, rechecks selection, computes, snapshots and appends from that same authoritative state. Deleted/deselected/stale cases cannot execute from the caller's old instance. Existing concurrent updates wait on that row. PATCH and POST remain separate requests: another client can save between them, so returned `input_snapshot` is authoritative. No optimistic revision or exactly-once network retry protocol is added.

nodes.label: 6. TDD and implementation boundary
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Apply test-first discrepancy tests to new extraction/comparison/reporting behavior; use controlled temporary inputs for drift and bad observations. Preserve meaningful red/green for new behavior and any reproduced product defect. Existing passing engine tests remain regressions. **Rationale**: A verification feature must demonstrate that it rejects wrong values and incomplete evidence; merely asserting equality on happy inputs is insufficient. Import/setup errors do not demonstrate a behavioral failure, and correct production formulas need no manufactured defect.

nodes.label: Assumptions
nodes.rationale: - Project tenancy, authentication, and project membership checks follow existing Velora patterns; new permission codes follow the established `view_*` / `edit_*` pairing (e.g. view/edit decision support) and are enforced server-side. - Phase 1 may create runs via a controlled stub/test path or “record run shell” that stores a frozen snapshot and empty/placeholder result so AC23–AC24 can be proven before engines exist; production “Run method” buttons for real engines arrive in later phases. - Weight normalization (`w[j] = weights[j] / sum(weights)`) is available as a shared pure helper for AC11; score computation is out of scope.

nodes.label: Assumptions
nodes.rationale: - Phase 1–2 case shell, shared validators, ranking editors, SAW engine, permissions, and project Decision Support route remain the host surface; TopsisMethodPanel is added alongside SawMethodPanel. - TOPSIS math is ported from the TOPSIS path of [09-ranking-reference.md](../../docs/decision-support/09-ranking-reference.md) and [04-topsis.md](../../docs/decision-support/04-topsis.md), as an independent callable (AC01). - Shared ranking validation from Phase 2 remains the first gate; TOPSIS adds all-zero column (denom) rejection and AC16 closeness rule.

nodes.label: Assumptions
nodes.rationale: - **Working policy for O07**: Use a fixed zero diagonal and allow finite decimal influences within 0–4. Each run uses one entered matrix. Multi-user judgment collection, weighting, and aggregation are outside this feature. These defaults are feature policy for planning, not a claim that the source resolved O07. - **Working policy for O08**: Block all-zero, singular, or numerically unreliable analyses with explicit feedback and no successful run. A one-criterion zero matrix is therefore structurally valid but not executable. There is no special zero-result outcome. Numerical techniques and stability thresholds must be documented during planning against this policy and the reference accuracy criterion. - **Role neutrality**: Treat an absolute relation of at most 10⁻⁹ as balanced to avoid presenting insignificant arithmetic residue as directional influence. Use the unrounded result for this classification. Retain the original signed numerical result in history; presentation rounding does not change it.

nodes.label: Assumptions
nodes.rationale: - **Working policy for O10**: Present a numbered layer list with explicit mutual-reachability group labels; accept cycles without deleting or splitting their members into artificial levels. An interactive layer diagram, layout rules and graph editing are deferred. This feature policy bounds the source's open presentation question without claiming O10 was resolved in the source documents. - **Direct diagonal policy**: Both binary zero and one are valid direct self-judgments. New drafts initialize the diagonal to explicit zero and leave off-diagonal judgments unanswered; users may change a direct diagonal to one. Derived self-reachability is always one and does not rewrite direct input or produce a multi-criterion cycle label by itself. - **Binary value policy**: Numeric zero and one, including numerically identical 0.0 and 1.0, are accepted. Text and booleans are not executable numeric judgments. Supported localized entry follows the existing shared input conventions and results in explicit binary judgments; no new global numeric/name normalization policy is introduced.

nodes.label: Assumptions
nodes.rationale: - This is a shared execution-record completion feature based on document 08, not the broader Phase 7 manual-transfer and whole-module acceptance project. Existing case/history and method-specific functionality is extended only where these requirements require it; working calculations are preserved. - Source inspection at specification time shows independent SAW, TOPSIS, AHP and ISM execution, stored history and method filtering already exist. AHP/ISM have readable historical output, while ranking history lacks equivalent method-specific review. This is a planning baseline, not a new behavioral acceptance claim; planning must verify it against the current workspace. - DEMATEL execution is currently a placeholder despite its existing specification. Implementing that engine belongs to feature 022. This feature must safely review placeholders and completed DEMATEL records when available; history-presentation checks can use fixed completed-record examples without claiming live DEMATEL calculation acceptance.

nodes.label: Assumptions
nodes.rationale: - Document 09 selects the reference responsibility. It requests no end-user code editor, second ranking engine, combined execution interface or downloadable calculation service. The existing editable document is the reference surface. - Source inspection shows independent SAW/TOPSIS calculations, method checks and shared records already exist. This is a planning baseline, not fresh behavioral acceptance. Planning must identify missing reference verification and reuse working capabilities and applicable evidence before proposing changes. - Dependencies are the [case shell](../018-decision-case-shell/spec.md), [SAW](../019-decision-saw/spec.md), [TOPSIS](../020-decision-topsis/spec.md), [execution records](../024-decision-execution-records/spec.md) and source documents above. An unavailable check does not authorize rebuilding earlier features.

nodes.label: ProjectChangeRequest — narrowly bind completed remediation
nodes.rationale: Keep CR's existing reason minimum, protected-field approval and SoD; group admin requester cannot self-final-approve, existing superuser exception unchanged. Update/submit/approve check binding, current state, current missing fields and fresh authority again under Project→CR locks. A completion-bound CR cannot be transplanted to an archive cycle, another completion, or active/suspended normal editing. While archived it is invalid for update/submit/approve even for an admin; archive round-trip back to the *same* completion may permit fresh current-context actions if all predicates still hold. An old signed undo preview is still invalid because version changed.

nodes.label: Decision 1 — Keep one authoritative five-value weather vocabulary
nodes.community_name: Research: Standardized Daily Weather and Temperature
nodes.norm_label: decision 1 — keep one authoritative five-value weather vocabulary
nodes.rationale: Separate enums for each model: rejected because the same project-day could acquire incompatible weather values.

nodes.label: Decision 2 — Treat committed normalization migrations as immutable and semantically forward-only
nodes.community_name: Research: Standardized Daily Weather and Temperature
nodes.norm_label: decision 2 — treat committed normalization migrations as immutable and semantically forward-only
nodes.rationale: Decision**: Preserve the committed ordered normalization: `sunny → clear`, `partly_cloudy → cloudy`, and `foggy → cloudy` in daily reports and weather logs, followed by the dependent specialty-report normalization. Because migrations `field_reports.0018_daily_header_weather` and `sub_reports.0004_standardize_weather` are already committed on `develop`, implementation MUST verify them rather than rewrite them. Any corrective schema/data work uses a new forward migration.

nodes.label: Decision 3 — Reject unknown new values and make aggregation deterministic for invalid or absent inputs
nodes.community_name: Research: Standardized Daily Weather and Temperature
nodes.norm_label: decision 3 — reject unknown new values and make aggregation deterministic for invalid or absent inputs
nodes.rationale: Give unknown values a severity of zero: rejected because they can still become the selected result.

nodes.label: Decision 4 — Enforce temperature rules through model metadata and effective-state API validation
nodes.community_name: Research: Standardized Daily Weather and Temperature
nodes.norm_label: decision 4 — enforce temperature rules through model metadata and effective-state api validation
nodes.rationale: Client-only validation: rejected because direct API and offline-sync writes bypass it.

nodes.label: Decision 5 — Use one client validator and gate every header write
nodes.community_name: Research: Standardized Daily Weather and Temperature
nodes.norm_label: decision 5 — use one client validator and gate every header write
nodes.rationale: Rely on native `min`/`max` attributes: rejected because programmatic and autosave writes do not necessarily trigger native form validation.

nodes.label: Decision 6 — Centralize the weather selector and consume localization keys
nodes.community_name: Research: Standardized Daily Weather and Temperature
nodes.norm_label: decision 6 — centralize the weather selector and consume localization keys
nodes.rationale: Keep separate option maps/selectors: rejected because label, order, and accepted-value drift has already occurred.

nodes.label: Decision 7 — Treat weather-impact notes as summary-owned plain text
nodes.community_name: Research: Standardized Daily Weather and Temperature
nodes.norm_label: decision 7 — treat weather-impact notes as summary-owned plain text
nodes.rationale: Derive or concatenate notes from specialty reports: rejected because no approved specialty source field exists.

nodes.label: Decision 8 — Normalize offline legacy values without accepting them as new server input
nodes.community_name: Research: Standardized Daily Weather and Temperature
nodes.norm_label: decision 8 — normalize offline legacy values without accepting them as new server input
nodes.rationale: Drop old cached/queued data: rejected because it loses user work.

nodes.label: FR-001: For EVM figures to be considered fully valid, the project MU
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: fr-001: for evm figures to be considered fully valid, the project mu
nodes.rationale: For EVM figures to be considered fully valid, the project MUST have defined and locked schedule and budget baselines; if either is unlocked, the system MUST show a clear “baseline is not locked” warning and MUST NOT present the report as fully valid.

nodes.label: FR-002: At a report cut-off (period or as-of date), the system MUST
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: fr-002: at a report cut-off (period or as-of date), the system must
nodes.rationale: At a report cut-off (period or as-of date), the system MUST compute or present PV, EV, and AC using the source definitions: PV = budgeted value of work planned; EV = budgeted value of work performed per the approved measurement method; AC = recorded actual cost.

nodes.label: FR-003: The system MUST present variances and indices including SV,
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: fr-003: the system must present variances and indices including sv,
nodes.rationale: The system MUST present variances and indices including SV, CV, SPI, CPI, and finish forecasts EAC, ETC, VAC using the common performance-based method when inputs allow.

nodes.label: FR-004: EVM numbers MUST be reportable at project, phase, and cost-c
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: fr-004: evm numbers must be reportable at project, phase, and cost-c
nodes.rationale: EVM numbers MUST be reportable at project, phase, and cost-center (CBS) levels and MUST support roll-up to project without silent double counting.

nodes.label: FR-005: When EV or AC is zero or absent in a way that makes a ratio
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: fr-005: when ev or ac is zero or absent in a way that makes a ratio
nodes.rationale: When EV or AC is zero or absent in a way that makes a ratio meaningless, CPI and/or SPI MUST be shown as “not computable” (localized), never as a fabricated numeric index.

nodes.label: FR-006: Missing or incomplete inputs (progress, cost, baseline, conv
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: fr-006: missing or incomplete inputs (progress, cost, baseline, conv
nodes.rationale: Missing or incomplete inputs (progress, cost, baseline, conversion) MUST be transparent in the EVM report—unregistered / incomplete / not computable—rather than a misleading numeric zero that implies measured performance.

nodes.label: FR-007: EV MUST be based on the approved measurement method from pro
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: fr-007: ev must be based on the approved measurement method from pro
nodes.rationale: EV MUST be based on the approved measurement method from progress/periodic reporting and MUST NOT be assumed equal to actual cost or invoice (IPC) amounts.

nodes.label: FR-008: When SPI or CPI is not computable, dependent forecasts (EAC,
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: fr-008: when spi or cpi is not computable, dependent forecasts (eac,
nodes.rationale: When SPI or CPI is not computable, dependent forecasts (EAC, ETC, VAC that rely on that index) MUST also be not computable.

nodes.label: FR-009: Changing the measurement method without the versioning/appro
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: fr-009: changing the measurement method without the versioning/appro
nodes.rationale: Changing the measurement method without the versioning/approval rules of progress reporting MUST NOT silently rewrite EVM history or create uncontrolled artificial variance; EVM MUST consume only approved/versioned progress outputs.

nodes.label: FR-010: Multi-currency aggregation MUST require explicit conversion;
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: fr-010: multi-currency aggregation must require explicit conversion;
nodes.rationale: Multi-currency aggregation MUST require explicit conversion; without it, the system MUST refuse silent cross-currency totals and state that clearly.

nodes.label: SC-001: For a seeded project with locked baselines, approved progres
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: sc-001: for a seeded project with locked baselines, approved progres
nodes.rationale: For a seeded project with locked baselines, approved progress, and actual cost, a project controller can open the EVM report at project level and see correct PV, EV, AC, SV, CV, and available SPI/CPI in under 2 minutes without a spreadsheet.

nodes.label: SC-002: In 100% of test cases with insufficient data for a ratio (mi
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: sc-002: in 100% of test cases with insufficient data for a ratio (mi
nodes.rationale: In 100% of test cases with insufficient data for a ratio (missing/zero EV or AC as defined), the dependent index is labeled not computable—never a misleading numeric value.

nodes.label: SC-003: Controllers can produce EVM at project, phase, and cost-cent
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: sc-003: controllers can produce evm at project, phase, and cost-cent
nodes.rationale: Controllers can produce EVM at project, phase, and cost-center (CBS) levels in the same product session, with project roll-up consistent with child slices under the defined aggregation rules.

nodes.label: SC-004: In 100% of test cases with an unlocked required baseline, th
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: sc-004: in 100% of test cases with an unlocked required baseline, th
nodes.rationale: In 100% of test cases with an unlocked required baseline, the report shows the baseline-not-locked warning and does not claim full validity.

nodes.label: SC-005: In 100% of tested cases, EV is not equal to AC or an invoice
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: sc-005: in 100% of tested cases, ev is not equal to ac or an invoice
nodes.rationale: In 100% of tested cases, EV is not equal to AC or an invoice amount solely because those amounts exist; EV follows the approved measurement method feed.

nodes.label: SC-006: When the measurement method changes without approval/version
nodes.community_name: Full Detail Serializer With Nested Items
nodes.norm_label: sc-006: when the measurement method changes without approval/version
nodes.rationale: When the measurement method changes without approval/versioning, historical EVM at prior cut-offs does not jump from an uncontrolled rewrite of progress inputs (verified by regression scenarios tied to progress versioning).

nodes.label: FR-001: Risk and issue MUST be separate entities (or clearly separat
nodes.norm_label: fr-001: risk and issue must be separate entities (or clearly separat
nodes.rationale: Risk and issue MUST be separate entities (or clearly separated record types with distinct lifecycle), not a single interchangeable “event” for both uncertain risk and realized issue.

nodes.label: FR-002: Each risk MUST support description, cause, consequence, prob
nodes.norm_label: fr-002: each risk must support description, cause, consequence, prob
nodes.rationale: Each risk MUST support description, cause, consequence, probability, impact severity, composite score (when computable), owner, response, action, due date, and status.

nodes.label: FR-003: Risk status MUST include at least: open, under review, mitig
nodes.norm_label: fr-003: risk status must include at least: open, under review, mitig
nodes.rationale: Risk status MUST include at least: open, under review, mitigated, closed, residual.

nodes.label: FR-004: Users MUST be able to link a risk to a related activity, cos
nodes.norm_label: fr-004: users must be able to link a risk to a related activity, cos
nodes.rationale: Users MUST be able to link a risk to a related activity, cost item, contract, and/or related decision when those targets exist on the project.

nodes.label: FR-005: The system MUST define reportable records for inspection pla
nodes.norm_label: fr-005: the system must define reportable records for inspection pla
nodes.rationale: The system MUST define reportable records for inspection plan/request/result, nonconformity, corrective action, work permit, training, incident, and near miss.

nodes.label: FR-006: Each inspection MUST be linked to a WBS node, a responsible
nodes.norm_label: fr-006: each inspection must be linked to a wbs node, a responsible
nodes.rationale: Each inspection MUST be linked to a WBS node, a responsible person, and a date; missing any of these MUST prevent a valid save.

nodes.label: FR-007: Users MUST be able to produce quality and safety reports at
nodes.norm_label: fr-007: users must be able to produce quality and safety reports at
nodes.rationale: Users MUST be able to produce quality and safety reports at project scope and for a selected time period.

nodes.label: FR-008: Impact dimensions for risk (at least schedule, cost, quality
nodes.norm_label: fr-008: impact dimensions for risk (at least schedule, cost, quality
nodes.rationale: Impact dimensions for risk (at least schedule, cost, quality, safety, contract, liquidity) MUST be filterable in the risk register.

nodes.label: FR-009: Closing a risk while related actions remain open MUST produc
nodes.norm_label: fr-009: closing a risk while related actions remain open must produc
nodes.rationale: Closing a risk while related actions remain open MUST produce a warning (acknowledge-to-proceed in v1).

nodes.label: FR-010: Composite score MUST NOT be invented when probability or imp
nodes.norm_label: fr-010: composite score must not be invented when probability or imp
nodes.rationale: Composite score MUST NOT be invented when probability or impact severity is missing.

nodes.label: SC-001: A project manager can register a risk with the required fiel
nodes.norm_label: sc-001: a project manager can register a risk with the required fiel
nodes.rationale: A project manager can register a risk with the required fields, change its status through the allowed set, and filter by at least one impact dimension in under 3 minutes on a seeded project.

nodes.label: SC-002: An issue recorded for an occurred event is distinguishable f
nodes.norm_label: sc-002: an issue recorded for an occurred event is distinguishable f
nodes.rationale: An issue recorded for an occurred event is distinguishable from an open risk in the same project register/views (no silent merge into one type).

nodes.label: SC-003: Quality/safety period report for a project returns inspectio
nodes.norm_label: sc-003: quality/safety period report for a project returns inspectio
nodes.rationale: Quality/safety period report for a project returns inspections, nonconformities, incidents, and near misses (and permits/training when present) for the selected range without requiring a spreadsheet export as the only path.

nodes.label: SC-004: In 100% of tested cases, an inspection cannot be saved witho
nodes.norm_label: sc-004: in 100% of tested cases, an inspection cannot be saved witho
nodes.rationale: In 100% of tested cases, an inspection cannot be saved without date and responsible person (and WBS).

nodes.label: SC-005: In 100% of tested cases with missing probability or impact s
nodes.norm_label: sc-005: in 100% of tested cases with missing probability or impact s
nodes.rationale: In 100% of tested cases with missing probability or impact severity, composite score is absent/not computed (not a fabricated number).

nodes.label: T088 account cache isolation
nodes.rationale: Two first eight-case UI attempts were GREEN because their assertions could complete before the destination route committed (and the first reason locator required exact text despite its label). Those results did not prove account isolation; no production guard was removed. Actual QueryClient inspection established cached detail/history and fixed freshness, then a robust post-route paint boundary/label-aware locator reproduced disclosure: 7 failed/1 passed in 32.7s, exit1, cache-final-red.log. A diagnostic single case also failed on the old actor text (cache-diagnostic.log). Cached and late-response cases use real SPA logout/login, same document marker, fixed clock within15s, and held B403 responses; they do not fabricate state mutations.

nodes.label: T091 sent-result and operation matrix
nodes.rationale: First targeted invocation: exit1,40 passed/4 operation-fixture timeouts (recovery-matrix.log); assumed a forward Complete control existed on suspended UI, which it does not. Did not add/remove a product control. A concurrent completion is now represented by new server DTO plus the actual singleton QueryClient refresh while both controllers stay mounted. Second invocation:24 fault cases passed/4 fixture timeouts because HMR had left the dynamically imported singleton URL separate from the mounted version. Restarted only the owned frontend to remove hot-module versioning; **4 operation cases passed (12.9s), exit0**, operation-green.log. This is setup correction, not behavior RED; no production workaround. All handler logic was already GREEN. Final full suite below reruns these together on the stable final server. T091 complete.

nodes.label: Assumptions
nodes.rationale: - **Saaty Scale Limits**: Comparisons are entered using the Saaty 1–9 preference scale and reciprocal fractions ($1/2 \dots 1/9$). Custom decimal inputs within $(0, 10)$ are supported for flexibility. - **CR Threshold**: The standard Saaty threshold $CR \le 0.10$ is accepted across construction and engineering management domains as the benchmark for acceptable consistency. - **Interim Warning Policy**: An inconsistent matrix ($CR > 0.10$) generates a valid run with `is_consistent: false` and a prominent UI warning rather than blocking the user from saving, allowing iterative exploration and history auditing.

nodes.label: 10x10 Maximum Dimension Boundary
nodes.rationale: Real matrix dimensions are dynamically user-defined with a hard upper bound of 10x10

nodes.label: Shared Input Validation Rules
nodes.rationale: Validates non-empty names, uniqueness, dimensions <= 10, non-negative finite numbers, non-zero cost criteria

nodes.label: Five-Step Method Execution Workflow
nodes.rationale: 1. Select method; 2. Form prepares inputs; 3. Validate; 4. Run engine; 5. Persist immutable result snapshot

nodes.label: Product Integration Seam
nodes.rationale: Specifies that UI and storage are responsibilities of the product development team, adhering to acceptance checks

nodes.label: AC14-AC22: Mathematical Formula Calculation Checks
nodes.rationale: Verifies numerical results of SAW, TOPSIS (ideal distances & closeness), AHP weights & CR, DEMATEL T & D+/-R, ISM reachability & layers

nodes.label: AC23-AC24: History and Immutable Snapshot Checks
nodes.norm_label: ac23-ac24: history and immutable snapshot checks
nodes.rationale: Verifies past execution history list and read-only frozen input snapshots

nodes.label: AC01-AC04: Method Selection & Independence Checks
nodes.rationale: Verifies standalone SAW, TOPSIS, AHP, DEMATEL, ISM runs and manual weight transfer

nodes.label: AC25-AC26: Result Display and Error Mapping Checks
nodes.norm_label: ac25-ac26: result display and error mapping checks
nodes.rationale: Verifies distinct result presentation and cell/field-targeted error reporting

nodes.label: AC05-AC13: Shared Inputs & Validation Checks
nodes.rationale: Verifies dimensions (1x1 to 10x10), rejection of non-numeric, empty, negative, and zero cost values

nodes.label: Decision Case Input Contract Specification
nodes.rationale: Defines case data schema and shared validation rules across all MCDM engines

nodes.label: Execution Records and Lifecycle Specification
nodes.rationale: Defines connection between decision case data, method engines, and result histories

nodes.label: Decision Support Acceptance Checks Specification
nodes.rationale: 26 formal acceptance checks (AC01-AC26) verifying method independence, validation, math, and audit records

nodes.label: Method Independence Principle
nodes.rationale: Each MCDM method runs strictly with its own inputs without requiring prior execution of another method

nodes.label: Immutable Run Snapshot (تصویر ثابت ورودی)
nodes.rationale: Frozen data record of inputs and results for auditability; editing a case never mutates past execution records

nodes.label: Independent Output Display Policy
nodes.rationale: Each method output is displayed separately; rankings from SAW and TOPSIS are never merged into a synthetic hybrid

nodes.label: Decision Support Clean Architecture Principles
nodes.rationale: Pure engines without UI, one matrix editor with adapters, thin routes, distinct ranking views, shared validation

nodes.label: rank_options Python Reference Function
nodes.rationale: Unified reference function calculating both SAW and TOPSIS scores on performance matrix

nodes.label: TOPSIS Euclidean Distance Metrics
nodes.rationale: S_i+ = sqrt(sum (v_ij - v_j^+)^2) and S_i- = sqrt(sum (v_ij - v_j^-)^2)

nodes.label: TOPSIS Positive and Negative Ideal Solutions
nodes.norm_label: topsis positive and negative ideal solutions
nodes.rationale: A+ (best: max for benefit, min for cost) and A- (worst: min for benefit, max for cost)

nodes.label: TOPSIS Method
nodes.rationale: Ranks alternatives based on geometric distances from positive and negative ideal solutions

nodes.label: TOPSIS Ranking Output
nodes.rationale: Sorted alternatives by C_i descending, including distances S_i+ and S_i-

nodes.label: TOPSIS Relative Closeness Score
nodes.rationale: C_i = S_i^- / (S_i^+ + S_i^-) with fallback C_i = 0.5 when S_i^+ + S_i^- == 0

nodes.label: TOPSIS Vector Normalization
nodes.rationale: r_ij = x_ij / sqrt(sum_{k=1}^m x_kj^2)

nodes.label: TOPSIS Weighted Normalized Matrix
nodes.rationale: v_ij = w_j * r_ij

nodes.label: Backend Decision Support Pure Calculation Services
nodes.norm_label: backend decision support pure calculation services
nodes.rationale: Pure calculation modules in apps/api/core/decision_support/ without HTTP or view coupling

nodes.label: R03: Wikipedia TOPSIS Overview
nodes.rationale: Online descriptive reference for TOPSIS method formulation

nodes.label: R07: Python Standard Library Documentation
nodes.rationale: Python 3 official library reference for mathematical built-ins

nodes.label: Scientific and Technical References Document
nodes.rationale: Scientific literature backing MCDM methods and implementation review status

nodes.label: R01: Avramova et al. 2025 (MCDM Industrial Overview)
nodes.norm_label: r01: avramova et al. 2025 (mcdm industrial overview)
nodes.rationale: Technologies 13(10), 444; Overview of MCDM methods in industry

nodes.label: R02: Hwang & Yoon 1981 (TOPSIS Foundations)
nodes.rationale: Multiple Attribute Decision Making: Methods and Applications (Springer)

nodes.label: R04: Taherdoost (AHP Step-by-Step Approach)
nodes.rationale: Decision Making Using Analytic Hierarchy Process (AHP) (HAL / Author intro)

nodes.label: R06: Chauhan et al. 2018 (ISM & DEMATEL Barriers Analysis)
nodes.norm_label: r06: chauhan et al. 2018 (ism & dematel barriers analysis)
nodes.rationale: Journal of the Air & Waste Management Association 68(2), 100-110

nodes.label: AHP Reciprocal Matrix Axiom
nodes.rationale: a_ji = 1 / a_ij and diagonal a_ii = 1

nodes.label: DEMATEL Direct Influence Scale 0-4
nodes.rationale: Direct influence scale: 0=no influence, 1=low, 2=medium, 3=high, 4=very high

nodes.label: DEMATEL Method
nodes.rationale: Causal analysis method determining influence intensity, prominence, and cause-effect roles

nodes.label: DEMATEL Matrix Normalization
nodes.rationale: s = max_{1<=i<=n} (sum_{j=1}^n M_ij); N = M / s

nodes.label: DEMATEL Prominence Index (D + R)
nodes.rationale: D_i = sum_j T_ij (dispatching); R_i = sum_j T_ji (receiving); Prominence = D + R indicates overall importance

nodes.label: DEMATEL Relation Index (D - R)
nodes.rationale: Relation = D - R; if positive, criterion is a net cause/driver; if negative, net effect/receiver

nodes.label: ISM Hierarchy Layers
nodes.rationale: Ordered levels from top (effects/outcomes) to bottom (fundamental root causes)

nodes.label: ISM Initial Reachability Matrix
nodes.rationale: M = A + I (boolean addition ensuring reflexive self-reachability M_ii = 1)

nodes.label: ISM Level Partitioning Condition
nodes.rationale: Criterion c_i is placed in current top level when R(c_i) = R(c_i) cap A(c_i), then removed iteratively

nodes.label: ISM Method (Interpretive Structural Modeling)
nodes.rationale: Transforms complex element relationships into a visible hierarchical structural model

nodes.label: ISM Reachability and Antecedent Sets
nodes.rationale: R(c_i) = reachability set; A(c_i) = antecedent set; intersection R(c_i) cap A(c_i)

nodes.label: ISM Transitive Reachability Matrix
nodes.rationale: M^* computed via boolean matrix multiplication until M^k = M^{k+1}

nodes.label: Mathematical Corrections from Source Audit
nodes.rationale: Corrects DEMATEL total relation matrix formula, ISM level condition R=R cap A, and AHP reciprocal matrix

nodes.label: ISM Method Calculation Specification
nodes.rationale: Mathematical formulas and level partitioning for Interpretive Structural Modeling

nodes.label: R05: Chen 2021 (Improved DEMATEL-ISM Integration)
nodes.rationale: PLOS ONE 16(7), e0254694; Validates DEMATEL total relation matrix and ISM level partitioning condition

nodes.label: Decision 10 — Excel-like UI (not pixel-perfect xlsx export)
nodes.norm_label: decision 10 — excel-like ui (not pixel-perfect xlsx export)
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Redesign project daily **view** into sectional layout matching the reference workbook sections (header, shifts, site status, weather, indirect/direct labor, materials, concrete, executed activities, general activities, issues, visits, approvals, management opinion). MVP **does not** require binary `.xlsx` export parity; PDF may remain existing path or follow later. **Rationale**: Spec assumptions; SC-003 sectional parity.

nodes.label: Decision 11 — Offline / sync create queue
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Project-level offline **create** of blank daily reports is out of line with FR-003. Offline queue may still sync **child edits on specialty** or summary metadata if already supported; do **not** enqueue new blank project daily creates from the removed button. Document any residual offline create paths as bugs to remove or redirect to specialty entry. **Rationale**: Avoid reintroducing create via syncService.

nodes.label: Decision 12 — Verification approach
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: pytest for rebuild sums/unions, status include/exclude, no blank create, permission isolation, metadata survival across rebuild; frontend typecheck; browser: list without create, ensure-by-date, specialty submit updates summary, incomplete banner, fa/en section labels. **Rationale**: Constitution VI.

nodes.label: Decision 1 — Materialized DailyReport as the summary shell
nodes.norm_label: decision 1 — materialized dailyreport as the summary shell
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Keep `field_reports.DailyReport` (unique current row per `project` + `report_date` + `shift=full`) as the **persisted project-day summary**. An aggregation service **ensures** the shell exists and **rebuilds derived child rows** from specialty sources. Do not introduce a separate `ProjectDailySummary` table. **Rationale**: Existing approval, PDF, navigation, progress, and child-row APIs already hang off `DailyReport`. Spec requires one logical report per day and automatic updates; materialization preserves those integrations (constitution V).

nodes.label: Decision 2 — Specialty source of truth
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: **Primary authoring surface** remains `sub_reports.DisciplineSubReport` (+ `DisciplineSubReportActivity` and additive specialty contribution structures for labor/materials/concrete as required to feed Excel sections). Aggregation includes sub-reports in statuses **`submitted` and `approved`** (exclude `draft` and `rejected` from the rebuild input set). On reject/delete/soft-delete, rebuild removes their contribution. **Rationale**: Spec FR-001/FR-006 and existing `linked_daily_report` FK already point at this relationship. Draft exclusion matches MVP assumption (“available for project visibility”).

nodes.label: Decision 3 — Gap: specialty models vs Excel sections
nodes.norm_label: decision 3 — gap: specialty models vs excel sections
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Today `DisciplineSubReport` mainly carries **activities + weather**. To satisfy FR-004, the feature **extends specialty contribution** so units can supply (as applicable to their discipline): labor present/leave by job title, material receipts, concrete pours, general activities, issues/visits narratives. Implementation may add child tables under `sub_reports` **or** map from existing project-date specialty entry surfaces if already authoritative—prefer extending `sub_reports` for a single rebuild input graph. Until a specialty section exists, the summary section renders **empty** and incompleteness messaging may note the gap—**not** reopened for free-form project-level create. **Rationale**: Spec requires Excel-like sections and specialty as source of truth; inventing project-level blank forms would reintroduce the removed create path.

nodes.label: Decision 4 — Rebuild trigger and ensure-by-date
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: 1. **On specialty write path** (create/update/submit/approve/reject/delete of a contributing sub-report or its contribution rows): call `rebuild_daily_report_summary(project_id, report_date)`. 2. **On project daily open by date**: `ensure_daily_report_summary(project_id, report_date)` get-or-creates the shell (shift=`full`) and runs rebuild if stale or never built.

nodes.label: Decision 5 — Remove project-level create UX (and constrain API)
nodes.norm_label: decision 5 — remove project-level create ux (and constrain api)
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Remove «گزارش جدید» / Plus create from `daily-reports-list` and retire `/daily-reports/new` as a blank-form entry. Replace with **open/ensure by date** (picker or row click → view/summary). API: prefer `GET/POST .../daily-reports/by-date/?date=` (or equivalent ensure action) over unrestricted blank `POST /daily-reports/`. Blank `POST` create for project daily reports is **disabled or restricted** to internal ensure (server-owned defaults only)—clients must not create empty authored reports. **Rationale**: FR-003/FR-011 explicitly forbid invite-to-create empty project daily reports.

nodes.label: Decision 6 — Derived rows read-only; summary metadata editable
nodes.norm_label: decision 6 — derived rows read-only; summary metadata editable
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: After a report is managed as an auto-summary, **PATCH/POST/DELETE on derived child collections** (activities, labor, materials, concrete, etc. that aggregation owns) returns a clear validation error. Allowed project-level mutations: weather/site **override** fields (optional), `general_notes` / issues narratives if designated summary-owned, **management opinion**, and existing **submit/review/approve/reject** workflow on the DailyReport shell. Rebuild **must not wipe** summary-owned metadata or approval timestamps. **Rationale**: FR-009 + assumptions; constitution IV safe mutations.

nodes.label: Decision 7 — Weather and site status reconciliation
nodes.norm_label: decision 7 — weather and site status reconciliation
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: 1. If project summary has an **explicit override** for weather or site status, keep it across rebuilds. 2. Else derive weather as the **most severe** among contributing sub-reports (severity order: stormy > snowy > rainy > foggy > cloudy > partly_cloudy > sunny; empty ignored).

nodes.label: Decision 8 — Labor and line-item aggregation rules
nodes.norm_label: decision 8 — labor and line-item aggregation rules
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: - **Labor**: sum `present` / `leave` (or shift counts / absence) **by** `(labor_category, job_title)` across contributing specialty labor rows. - **Activities / materials / concrete / general**: **union** of contribution rows into DailyReport child tables, copying description, shift, contractor, headcount, zone/block/floor, quantity, unit, notes; set provenance (`source_sub_report`, `source_discipline`).

nodes.label: Decision 9 — Incompleteness banner
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Summary payload includes `contributing_disciplines`, `missing_disciplines` (configured expected set minus submitted/approved for that date), and `is_partial`. UI shows a banner when `is_partial`. Expected discipline set = project-configured list or all `Discipline` enum values enabled for the project (default: civil, electrical, mechanical if project has no config). **Rationale**: FR-012.

nodes.label: Decision 10 — Compatibility corpus
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Add fixtures under `apps/api/core/schedule/tests/fixtures/mpp/` (and paired XML where applicable): hierarchy, milestones, dependencies, dates/durations/progress, critical/slack when present, plus rejection set (corrupt, wrong content + `.mpp` name, password-protected, oversized stub, unreadable genuine MPP). Prefer generating paired XML via MPXJ from the same MPP for SC-003, checked into fixtures once stable. **Rationale**: FR-021, SC-002, SC-003, SC-004.

nodes.label: Decision 11 — Permissions unchanged
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Preview/start remain `edit_wbs`; status poll remains project-scoped job lookup (`project_id` + job pk) with existing `view_wbs` / membership checks as today. No cross-project file or job access. **Rationale**: FR-018; constitution I.

nodes.label: Decision 1 — Processing strategy: MPP → MSPDI XML → existing MSP parser
nodes.norm_label: decision 1 — processing strategy: mpp → mspdi xml → existing msp parser
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Read genuine `.mpp` bytes with a bounded converter, produce in-memory Microsoft Project XML (MSPDI), then feed that XML into the existing `parse_msp_xml` → `build_preview` / `execute_msp_import` pipeline. Do not invent a second WBS/activity mapping model. **Rationale**: Spec FR-004–FR-006 and SC-003 require MPP and MSP XML equivalence for supported fields and the same summary→WBS / leaf→activity presentation. Reusing the proven XML importer maximizes parity and satisfies constitution V (minimal coherent change).

nodes.label: Decision 2 — Converter library: MPXJ (Python package + JVM)
nodes.norm_label: decision 2 — converter library: mpxj (python package + jvm)
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Use the open-source **MPXJ** stack to read MPP and write MSPDI XML. Prefer PyPI `mpxj` via JPype when installed; otherwise fall back to a **Java CLI** classpath (`MPP_MPXJ_CLASSPATH` / `net.sf.mpxj.sample.MpxjConvert`). Runtime requires a compatible **JRE**. Prefer lazy JVM start once per process when using JPype; never start/stop JVM per request. **Rationale**: MPXJ reads MPP8/9/12/14 generations (Project 98 through modern Microsoft 365 binaries)—aligned with FR-022 best-effort policy. Password-protected files raise a distinct “File is password protected” exception usable for FR-013. LGPL-compatible for server-side use; widely used for schedule interchange.

nodes.label: Decision 3 — Password policy: reject, never bypass
nodes.norm_label: decision 3 — password policy: reject, never bypass
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: On password-protected MPP, return the specific `mpp_password_protected` error. Do **not** call MPXJ options that ignore password protection (e.g. `setRespectPasswordProtection(false)`), even for MPP9 where bypass is technically possible. **Rationale**: Spec out-of-scope and FR-010 explicitly forbid recovering/bypassing passwords. Constitution IV safe mutations / untrusted input.

nodes.label: Decision 4 — Content validation before conversion
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Extend schedule upload validation to allow `.mpp` in addition to `.xml` for the MSP import endpoints. Enforce 50 MB size. Detect content with `python-magic` (and/or OLE compound-document signature `D0 CF 11 E0…`) rather than trusting client MIME/extension alone. Extension `.mpp` with non-OLE/non-MPP content → `invalid_file_type` or `mpp_corrupt` as appropriate. True OLE that is not a readable Project file → `mpp_corrupt` / `mpp_unsupported` after converter fails to recognize Project structure. **Rationale**: FR-008, FR-009, FR-013; existing `validate_upload` / `python-magic` pattern in `common.validators`.

nodes.label: Decision 5 — API surface: extend MSP import, not a third family
nodes.norm_label: decision 5 — api surface: extend msp import, not a third family
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Keep existing routes under `/api/v1/projects/{id}/import/msp/` for both `.xml` and `.mpp`. P6 remains `/import/p6/` for `.xer`. Server dispatches on validated content/extension: XML → current path; MPP → convert then current path. Reuse `MspImportJob` for both. **Rationale**: Spec says same wizard and same MSP workflow; constitution V. Frontend already branches XER vs MSP by extension; extend MSP branch to include `.mpp`.

nodes.label: Decision 6 — Error taxonomy (stable codes + localized messages)
nodes.norm_label: decision 6 — error taxonomy (stable codes + localized messages)
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Introduce stable machine-readable **error codes** (language-independent) with localized `message` strings: | Code | When |

nodes.label: Decision 7 — Time/resource bounds
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: - Hard wall-clock timeout for MPP conversion (recommended default **60s**, configurable via settings env). - On timeout: terminate conversion work cleanly, return `processing_timeout`, no project mutation; do not leave JVM/thread in a state that blocks later imports.

nodes.label: Decision 8 — Atomicity
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Keep `execute_msp_import` `@transaction.atomic`. Conversion happens **before** any WBS/activity writes (preview always; import job converts then executes). If conversion fails, job → `failed` with code; project rows unchanged. Mid-execute failure rolls back transactional mutations; baseline/relations created only inside the same transaction as today. **Rationale**: FR-010, FR-011, SC-004.

nodes.label: Decision 9 — Frontend routing and UX
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Update `msp-import-wizard.tsx` and `msp.ts`: - Accept `.mpp` in picker, drag-drop, and client pre-check. - Route `.xer` → P6; `.xml` and `.mpp` → MSP endpoints.

nodes.label: Evidence boundary
nodes.rationale: Read-only backend and frontend research agents inspected current source, related contracts and tests. The existing graphify index located `execution_service.py`, `DecisionRun`, `InputSnapshotViewer` and history/ranking components; its query was truncated and its indexed line numbers differ from current source. Current files, not graph edges, establish the baseline below. No graph rebuild or package update was performed. No application suites or live mutations were run during planning. Runtime inspection confirmed Python 3.12.3, Django 4.2.11 and Node 25.2.1. Prior feature 023 retains 205 backend, 70 helper and 78 browser passes; these are earlier evidence, not acceptance of feature 024.

nodes.label: R2 — Lock the authoritative parent before all execution decisions
nodes.norm_label: r2 — lock the authoritative parent before all execution decisions
nodes.rationale: - **Decision**: In `services/execution_service.py`, move all supported dispatch through one `transaction.atomic` boundary that loads the active, project-scoped `DecisionCase` with `select_for_update`, then checks method selection, validates, computes, deep-copies inputs and appends. Preserve current engine calls and method result shapes. Remove redundant ISM-only transaction orchestration once the common boundary owns it. - **Rationale**: Current `create_run` uses the supplied instance for SAW/TOPSIS/AHP/DEMATEL-placeholder; only `_create_ism_run` reloads and locks. This proves a stale-instance eligibility/input/deletion gap, not that every current output necessarily mixes states. Django locks evaluated rows through transaction completion; PostgreSQL transaction-capable tests are needed to verify contention. [Django 4.2 locking documentation](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/4.2/ref/models/querysets/#select-for-update). - **Alternatives considered**: `atomic` without reload/lock cannot establish authoritative eligibility. Optimistic revisions and cross-request PATCH→POST atomicity exceed this spec. A POST uses one persisted case state at lock acquisition; it does not promise the exact earlier browser draft if another user edited between requests.

nodes.label: R6 — Generalize the existing save–execute–recover boundary
nodes.norm_label: r6 — generalize the existing save–execute–recover boundary
nodes.rationale: - **Decision**: Extract a bounded recovery helper and thin `useDecisionExecution` hook from ISM's established orchestration for SAW/TOPSIS/AHP/ISM. Keep method-specific draft validation, payload construction and presentation in their panels. Use the route's existing per-case `beginOperation`; captured IDs and release callback remain authoritative. Guard global create/PATCH save responses before route callbacks too. - **Rationale**: ISM validates responses before release and awaits history recovery. Other panels release immediately after PATCH/POST, may retain stale output, and lack awaited recovery. A shared four-panel operation boundary is a small coherent reuse, not a second state framework. - **Alternatives considered**: Four duplicated recovery flows would drift. A global busy flag would block unrelated cases. Automatic POST retries, idempotency keys and revisions are outside scope.

nodes.label: Decision 10 — Verification approach
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: pytest for stakeholder filter, department activity write/filter/import validation, project isolation; frontend typecheck; browser check of department activity modal + ذینفعان role + at least one P2 surface; fa/en labels for role and empty state. **Rationale**: Constitution VI — domain field change spans models, API, UI, import.

nodes.label: Decision 1 — Source of contractor identity
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Project `Stakeholder` rows classified as contractors are the sole source for in-scope پیمانکار pickers. **Rationale**: Spec FR-002/FR-003 name ذینفعان explicitly. The separate `subcontractors` app and `contracts.Contract` lists are different domains (performance / commercial), not the stakeholder register.

nodes.label: Decision 2 — How a stakeholder is classified as contractor
nodes.norm_label: decision 2 — how a stakeholder is classified as contractor
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Canonical `role` value `contractor` on `projects.Stakeholder`. Writes that use Persian label `پیمانکار` (or common English synonyms) normalize to `contractor`. List/filter uses `role=contractor` plus `status=active` (and soft-delete exclusion). ذینفعان UI exposes a role control that includes contractor. **Rationale**: `role` already exists on the model and serializer; no new column required for classification. Stable English code keeps API/filter language-independent (constitution III). Normalization avoids duplicate spellings breaking FR-008 filters.

nodes.label: Decision 3 — Durable link + display name
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: In-scope operational models gain a nullable FK to `projects.Stakeholder` (SET_NULL on delete). Existing CharField name columns remain as a denormalized display snapshot written on save from the stakeholder’s `name`. New writes require a valid active contractor FK (except warehouse department rows that already clear contractor). Reads always prefer snapshot name for history (FR-006). **Rationale**: Satisfies FR-005 (identity) and FR-006 (stable display after inactive/delete). Avoids JOIN-only display that would blank after soft-delete if names were not snapshotted.

nodes.label: Decision 4 — Department activity (P1 surface)
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Add `contractor_ref` → `Stakeholder` on `DepartmentActivityRecord`. Serializer accepts `contractor_ref` (UUID); validates same-project, role=contractor, active, not soft-deleted; sets `contractor` from stakeholder name. Filter query param may accept stakeholder UUID and/or name contains for backward compat. Import resolves پیمانکار cell to an existing contractor by exact name (case-trimmed) or UUID; otherwise row fails validation. **Rationale**: Primary reported UI (`department-activity-record-modal`) today is a required free-text Input. This is the P1 path.

nodes.label: Decision 5 — Daily report / labor (P2 surfaces)
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Stop using `contracts` list for the پیمانکار combo. Add `contractor_ref` → `Stakeholder` on `DailyReportActivity` and labor-camp entry models that expose `subcontractor_name`. Keep legacy `subcontractor_ref` → `Contract` nullable and unused by the new picker (no destructive drop in v1). On save, set `subcontractor_name` from the chosen stakeholder. UI options come from the same contractors endpoint/filter as department activity. **Rationale**: Spec FR-009 includes these labels. Changing the existing Contract FK type would break migrations and any stored links; additive Stakeholder FK is safer (constitution II/V).

nodes.label: Decision 6 — Project settings / create wizard پیمانکار
nodes.norm_label: decision 6 — project settings / create wizard پیمانکار
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Treat as in-scope party picker: add optional `contractor_ref` → Stakeholder on `Project`; sync `Project.contractor` CharField from selected name. Empty selection clears the FK and may clear or leave CharField empty per existing blank rules. **Rationale**: Matches spec assumption default; same control pattern as operational forms.

nodes.label: Decision 7 — API shape for options
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Extend existing `GET /api/v1/projects/{id}/stakeholders/?role=contractor&status=active` (paginated `results` already). Frontend shared helper `fetchProjectContractors(projectId)` wraps that filter. No new micro-resource required for v1; optional thin alias endpoint may be added later if list payload is too heavy (contacts redaction already applies). **Rationale**: Minimal coherent change (constitution V); reuses ACL and redaction rules.

nodes.label: Decision 8 — UI control
nodes.rationale: **Decision**: Shared non-creatable select/combobox (existing `Select` or searchable non-add combobox). Do **not** use `CreatableSelect` for پیمانکار (that component’s Add path violates FR-007). Empty state copy points users to ذینفعان. Role field added on stakeholders create/edit form with contractor option labeled پیمانکار. **Rationale**: Constitution VII requires accessible selects; creatable “Add” is explicitly wrong for this field.

nodes.label: Source-discipline compatibility

nodes.label: ActivityMeasurementDefinition
nodes.rationale: Current measurement setup for one activity defining method (quantity, weighted_milestones, evidence_percent), basis, and status.

nodes.label: ActivityMeasurementVersion
nodes.rationale: Immutable snapshot created on each measurement approval maintaining version number and historical basis.

nodes.label: ActivityProgress Extended Model
nodes.rationale: Progress record storing period_progress, approved_progress, technical approval metadata, and link to measurement version.

nodes.label: ActivityQuantityChange
nodes.rationale: Approved basis quantity increase allowing progress to exceed prior 100% up to new total.

nodes.label: Measurement Definition State Machine
nodes.rationale: Draft to Approved (version N), with subsequent changes requiring new draft and re-approval (version N+1).

nodes.label: Progress & Report Validation Rules
nodes.rationale: Validation codes: measurement_not_approved, incomplete_measurement_basis, progress_exceeds_100, photo_not_technical_approval, figure_immutable, method_change_reason_required.

nodes.label: Manual Progress Entry Endpoint
nodes.rationale: POST /progress/manual/ requiring approved measurement definition and enforcing strict reject on >100%.

nodes.label: Activity Measurement Methods Endpoints
nodes.rationale: Endpoints /activities/{id}/measurement/ and /quantity-changes/ for defining, approving, and updating measurement basis.

nodes.label: Data Model: Physical Progress & Periodic Reports
nodes.norm_label: data model: physical progress & periodic reports
nodes.rationale: Data model definition for physical progress measurement methods, versioning, periodic reports, and figures.

nodes.label: FR-PRG Gap Analysis
nodes.rationale: Mapping of 11 functional requirements (FR-PRG-001 to FR-PRG-011) from current state to target gaps.

nodes.label: User Story 2: Distinct Four-Way Progress Display
nodes.norm_label: user story 2: distinct four-way progress display
nodes.rationale: PM sees period, cumulative, planned, and approved progress as 4 separate labeled metrics without conflation.

nodes.label: User Story 3: Generate Weekly and Monthly Reports
nodes.norm_label: user story 3: generate weekly and monthly reports
nodes.rationale: Generate weekly reports from approved dailies and monthly reports from multidisciplinary modules with figure provenance.

nodes.label: User Story 1: Record Progress with Approved Measurement Method
nodes.norm_label: user story 1: record progress with approved measurement method
nodes.rationale: Controls engineer selects quantity, milestone, or evidence method with approved basis before reporting.

nodes.label: User Story 4: Versioned Measurement Method Change
nodes.norm_label: user story 4: versioned measurement method change
nodes.rationale: Modifying measurement method creates a new pending version requiring approval while preserving auditability of historical records.

nodes.label: Feature Specification: Physical Progress & Periodic Reports Gap Closure
nodes.norm_label: feature specification: physical progress & periodic reports gap closure
nodes.rationale: Spec 009 defining gap closure against FR-PRG for physical progress measurement and periodic report rollup.

nodes.label: Strict Anti-Clamping Progress Rejection Rule
nodes.rationale: Progress > 100% must be rejected immediately rather than silently clamped to 100%, unless an approved quantity change exists.

nodes.label: Report Figure Provenance & Audit Requirement
nodes.rationale: Every figure on weekly/monthly reports must link directly to source records and modification without an override record is forbidden.

nodes.label: Photo Evidence Separation from Technical Approval
nodes.norm_label: photo evidence separation from technical approval
nodes.rationale: Photo attachment acts purely as operational evidence and never automatically confers technical progress approval.

nodes.label: Commitment Remaining Balance
nodes.rationale: Derived remaining balance calculated as commitment amount minus posted valid payments.

nodes.label: Actual vs Projected Series Separation
nodes.rationale: Keeps actual ledger transactions (CashTransaction) completely separate from dynamically projected series.

nodes.label: Monthly Net Need Calculation
nodes.rationale: Monthly net need = projected_inflow - projected_outflow (or shortfall when outflow exceeds inflow).

nodes.label: Projected Inflow Feed (IPC Receivables)
nodes.rationale: Projected inflow derived dynamically from approved unpaid IPC receivables grouped by due date month.

nodes.label: Projected Outflow Feed (Commitment Dues)
nodes.rationale: Projected outflow derived dynamically from open commitments (amount - posted payments) grouped by due date month.

nodes.label: Projected Cash Series API
nodes.rationale: GET /api/v1/projects/{project_id}/cash-flow/projection/ returning monthly projected inflow, outflow, and net need.

nodes.label: FR-CASH-001: Forecast vs Actual Separation
nodes.rationale: Requirement: Projected and actual cash series must be reported separately per project without mixing.

nodes.label: FR-CASH-003: Monthly Net Cash Need
nodes.rationale: Requirement: Monthly net cash need computed as monthly projected inflow minus projected outflow.

nodes.label: Decision 1: Dynamic Computed Projections on Read
nodes.norm_label: decision 1: dynamic computed projections on read
nodes.rationale: Computes projected series on-the-fly from live IPC receivables and commitments rather than writing ghost transactions.

nodes.label: Double Allocation Warning & Overlap Ack
nodes.rationale: Detects overlapping allocations across cycles/dates; returns 400 overlapping_allocation unless acknowledge_overlap=true.

nodes.label: Liquidity Decision Save API
nodes.rationale: POST .../cycles/{id}/decisions/ recording owner, rationale, schedule impact, and cost impact for audit history.

nodes.label: LiquidityAllocationDecision Model
nodes.rationale: Model storing owner, rationale, acknowledge_overlap flag, and created_at timestamp for audited governance.

nodes.label: LiquidityAllocationLine Model
nodes.rationale: Model linking decision to project with amount, period dates, schedule_impact, and cost_impact notes.

nodes.label: FR-CASH-007: Decision Governance Audit Trail
nodes.rationale: Requirement: Final allocation decisions require named owner and rationale, preserved as audit history.

nodes.label: FR-CASH-008: Double Allocation Warning & Simulation
nodes.rationale: Requirement: Warns on overlapping allocations and supports manual simulation scenarios with impact tracking.

nodes.label: FR-CASH-010: Manual Forecast Preservation
nodes.rationale: Requirement: Existing manual forecasts remain available side-by-side and are not overwritten by computed projections.

nodes.label: Spec 013: Cash Flow & Liquidity Allocation Gap Closure
nodes.norm_label: spec 013: cash flow & liquidity allocation gap closure
nodes.rationale: Specification closing FR-CASH gaps for project cash projections, net cash need, priority scoring, portfolio allocation, and audit governance.

nodes.label: FR-BUD Multi-Level Budget Requirements
nodes.rationale: Specifies requirements for budget versions, multi-level line allocations (WBS, CBS, Phase, Contract), approved changes, and ceiling limits.

nodes.label: User Story 1: Register and Submit Initial Budget for Approval
nodes.norm_label: user story 1: register and submit initial budget for approval
nodes.rationale: Allows project teams to register multi-level budget lines across project/phase/wbs/cbs/contract and submit for formal approval.

nodes.label: User Story 2: Budget Change Only via Approved Workflow
nodes.norm_label: user story 2: budget change only via approved workflow
nodes.rationale: Ensures approved budget baseline rows cannot be directly modified or deleted without a formal BudgetChangeRequest.

nodes.label: User Story 3: Remaining Allocatable and Controlled Transfers
nodes.norm_label: user story 3: remaining allocatable and controlled transfers
nodes.rationale: Computes remaining allocatable funds against commitments and actual costs, supporting zero-sum transfers between lines.

nodes.label: Contract: IPC Submitted vs Approved Amounts API
nodes.norm_label: contract: ipc submitted vs approved amounts api
nodes.rationale: Defines field behavior and mutability across IPC states (gross_amount, submitted_amount, approved_amount, approval_variance_note).

nodes.label: Contract: Payment Terms API & UI
nodes.rationale: Specifies contract create/update payload with payment_terms string and UI multiline textarea.

nodes.label: Contract Model Extensions (Payment Terms)
nodes.rationale: Adds payment_terms free-text field to Contract model while preserving number, title, amount, retention, and advance percentages.

nodes.label: IPC Model Extensions (Submitted & Approved Amounts)
nodes.rationale: Extends IPC model with submitted_amount (frozen on submit), approved_amount (set on approve <= submitted), and approval_variance_note.

nodes.label: User Story 2: IPC Cycle (Submit, Approve Amounts, and Partial Collections)
nodes.norm_label: user story 2: ipc cycle (submit, approve amounts, and partial collections)
nodes.rationale: Distinguishes contractor gross submitted amount from employer approved amount, requiring variance notes when reduced, without mutating status on collection.

nodes.label: R1 Research Decision: Version Model vs Mutable Rows
nodes.norm_label: r1 research decision: version model vs mutable rows
nodes.rationale: Introduce BudgetVersion as unit of approval. Rejected soft-history triggers and separate snapshot JSON to maintain relational integrity and auditability.

nodes.label: R2 Research Decision: Control Baseline for Ceiling Enforcement
nodes.norm_label: r2 research decision: control baseline for ceiling enforcement
nodes.rationale: Active project budget ceiling is defined by the latest approved control version (status=approved, kind in approved/revised).

nodes.label: R3 Research Decision: Phase Level Without Dedicated Phase Table
nodes.norm_label: r3 research decision: phase level without dedicated phase table
nodes.rationale: Reuses WBS structure for level=phase lines instead of introducing a separate Phase master table.

nodes.label: R4 Research Decision: Change Request vs Transfer Distinction
nodes.norm_label: r4 research decision: change request vs transfer distinction
nodes.rationale: BudgetChangeRequest is mandatory when total budget changes or baseline is altered; BudgetTransfer handles internal net-zero reallocations.

nodes.label: R5 Research Decision: Remaining Calculation Formula
nodes.norm_label: r5 research decision: remaining calculation formula
nodes.rationale: Remaining = approved_amount - committed - consumed per heading key. Prevents negative display by flooring at 0 and flagging overrun=true.

nodes.label: R6 Research Decision: Legacy Budget Rows Migration
nodes.norm_label: r6 research decision: legacy budget rows migration
nodes.rationale: Backfills existing orphan Budget rows into a synthesized default BudgetVersion per project to prevent regressions.

nodes.label: IPC Collection Status Invariant
nodes.rationale: Strict architectural invariant: partial or full collections recorded against an IPC must NEVER mutate its approval status or approved amount.

nodes.label: Research Decision: Split Submitted and Approved Amount Fields
nodes.norm_label: research decision: split submitted and approved amount fields
nodes.rationale: Adding dedicated DecimalFields submitted_amount and approved_amount preserves both contractor submission and employer approved amount without data loss.

nodes.label: Research Decision: No Auto-Transition to Paid on Collection
nodes.norm_label: research decision: no auto-transition to paid on collection
nodes.rationale: Preserves FR-CON-003: Collections represent cash movements; IPC status transition to paid remains an explicit action.

nodes.label: Research Decision: Amount Snapshot Timing & Variance Note
nodes.norm_label: research decision: amount snapshot timing & variance note
nodes.rationale: Freeze submitted_amount on submit; set approved_amount on approve. Require approval_variance_note whenever approved < submitted for auditability.

nodes.norm_label: user story 2 - correction request for locked reports (priority: p1)

As a site supervisor or project manager, once a report is approved (locked), nobody can edit it directly. Corrections require a correction request with a reason; the previous approved version is retained and a new editable version proceeds through approval again.

**Why this priority**: FR-DR-008 / SC-DR-003 are the largest compliance gaps; edit-block alone is insufficient without a lawful amend p

As a project controls engineer, I define a schedule activity on a WBS package with working calendar, duration (including milestone = zero), planned dates, forecast dates, predecessors, responsible person, and status—so planned, actual, and forecast stay distinct.

**Why this priority**: Closes FR-SCH-001 and FR-SCH-004; without calendar/duration/forecast, SC-SCH-003 cannot be met.

nodes.label: User Story 2 - Lock approved baseline and protect deviation history (Priority: P1)
nodes.norm_label: user story 2 - lock approved baseline and protect deviation history (priority: p1)
nodes.rationale:
As a project manager, after I approve a baseline I expect it to be locked. Updating the live schedule must not rewrite the locked snapshot; I can still compare approved vs current.

**Why this priority**: FR-SCH-005 / SC-SCH-002; without lock, “baseline” is only a mutable label and deviation history is unreliable.

**Independent Test**: Approve and lock a baseline; change a live activity’s planned

nodes.label: User Story 3 - Schedule change request with impact and new baseline version (Priority: P1)
nodes.norm_label: user story 3 - schedule change request with impact and new baseline version (priority: p1)
nodes.rationale:
As a project controls engineer, I submit a schedule change request with reason, impacts on milestones/cost/contract, and an approver path. On approval, a new locked baseline version is created without erasing the prior locked version.

**Why this priority**: FR-SCH-006 is entirely missing; it is the only compliant path to change an approved program.

**Independent Test**: Open a change request aga

nodes.label: User Story 4 - Milestone, delay, and critical-path validity report (Priority: P2)
nodes.norm_label: user story 4 - milestone, delay, and critical-path validity report (priority: p2)
nodes.rationale:
As a project manager, I open a schedule status report that lists milestones, critical and near-critical activities, delays, and forecast project finish—and if durations or relations are incomplete, critical path is labeled not valid / not calculable instead of showing a false path.

**Why this priority**: FR-SCH-007 / FR-SCH-008 / SC-SCH-004; misleading critical flags undermine control decisions.

nodes.label: EVM Metric: Actual Cost (AC)

nodes.label: EVM Metric: Cost Performance Index (CPI)
nodes.rationale: Formula: EV / AC

nodes.label: EVM Metric: Cost Variance (CV)
nodes.rationale: Formula: EV - AC

nodes.label: EVM Metric: Estimate At Completion (EAC)
nodes.rationale: Formula: BAC / CPI

nodes.label: EVM Metric: Estimate To Complete (ETC)
nodes.rationale: Formula: EAC - AC

nodes.label: EVM Metric: Earned Value (EV)
nodes.rationale: Formula: BAC_scope * approved_progress_scope

nodes.rationale: Formula: BAC_scope * planned_progress_scope

nodes.label: EVM Metric: Schedule Performance Index (SPI)
nodes.rationale: Formula: EV / PV

nodes.label: EVM Metric: Schedule Variance (SV)
nodes.rationale: Formula: EV - PV

nodes.label: EVM Metric: Variance At Completion (VAC)
nodes.rationale: Formula: BAC - EAC

nodes.label: Activity Relation
nodes.rationale: Predecessor/successor link with type and lag.

nodes.label: Schedule Activity
nodes.rationale: Time-bounded work item on a WBS package; holds planned, actual, and forecast dates; duration; optional milestone marker; calendar; owner; status.

nodes.label: Schedule Baseline
nodes.rationale: Named, approvable, lockable snapshot of activity dates/quantities for deviation history; one current locked baseline per project at a time after approval.

nodes.label: Schedule Change Request
nodes.rationale: Controlled proposal to alter the approved program; on approval produces a new baseline version.

nodes.label: Schedule Status Report
nodes.rationale: Read model listing milestones, critical/near-critical (if valid), delays, and forecast finish with four-way date clarity.

nodes.label: Working Calendar
nodes.rationale: Project (or shared) definition of working/non-working days used to validate activity dates.

nodes.label: FR-001: A schedule activity MUST remain linked to exactly one WBS pa
nodes.norm_label: fr-001: a schedule activity must remain linked to exactly one wbs pa
nodes.rationale: A schedule activity MUST remain linked to exactly one WBS package and MUST support title, duration (including zero for milestones), planned start/finish, working calendar reference, predecessors, responsible person, planned quantity or weight, and status.

nodes.label: FR-002: Predecessor relations MUST continue to support at least fini
nodes.norm_label: fr-002: predecessor relations must continue to support at least fini
nodes.rationale: Predecessor relations MUST continue to support at least finish-to-start; SS/FF/SF remain allowed with lag; cycle creation MUST be rejected.

nodes.label: FR-003: The system MUST detect and reject or clearly warn on impossi
nodes.norm_label: fr-003: the system must detect and reject or clearly warn on impossi
nodes.rationale: The system MUST detect and reject or clearly warn on impossible dates (finish before start; dates inconsistent with the activity’s working calendar) and MUST continue to reject dependency cycles; activities without WBS MUST not be publishable (WBS remains mandatory).

nodes.label: FR-004: Planned dates, actual dates, and forecast dates MUST be stor
nodes.norm_label: fr-004: planned dates, actual dates, and forecast dates must be stor
nodes.rationale: Planned dates, actual dates, and forecast dates MUST be stored and presented as separate values; updating one MUST NOT overwrite another.

nodes.label: FR-005: An approved schedule baseline MUST be lockable; locked basel
nodes.norm_label: fr-005: an approved schedule baseline must be lockable; locked basel
nodes.rationale: An approved schedule baseline MUST be lockable; locked baseline snapshot data MUST NOT be rewritten by live schedule edits; prior baseline versions MUST remain for deviation history.

nodes.label: FR-006: A schedule change request MUST capture reason, impacts on mi
nodes.norm_label: fr-006: a schedule change request must capture reason, impacts on mi
nodes.rationale: A schedule change request MUST capture reason, impacts on milestones, cost, and contract, requester, and approver outcome; approval MUST create a new baseline version without destroying the previous locked version.

nodes.label: FR-007: A schedule status report MUST present milestones, critical a
nodes.norm_label: fr-007: a schedule status report must present milestones, critical a
nodes.rationale: A schedule status report MUST present milestones, critical and near-critical activities (when path is valid), delays, and forecast finish, and MUST show approved / current / actual / forecast distinctly where data exists.

nodes.label: FR-008: Critical-path results MUST be marked not calculable / not va
nodes.norm_label: fr-008: critical-path results must be marked not calculable / not va
nodes.rationale: Critical-path results MUST be marked not calculable / not valid when required durations or relations are incomplete; the product MUST NOT present an authoritative critical path from incomplete data.

nodes.label: FR-009: Soft-delete and audit expectations from core principles MUST
nodes.norm_label: fr-009: soft-delete and audit expectations from core principles must
nodes.rationale: Soft-delete and audit expectations from core principles MUST apply to activities, relations, baselines, and change requests (who/when; no silent hard-delete of approved baseline history).

nodes.label: SC-001: A controls user can create two FS-linked activities with cal
nodes.norm_label: sc-001: a controls user can create two fs-linked activities with cal
nodes.rationale: A controls user can create two FS-linked activities with calendar, duration, and distinct forecast dates, and a zero-duration milestone, in one session without losing separation of planned/actual/forecast.

nodes.label: SC-002: In 100% of automated checks, editing live planned dates afte
nodes.norm_label: sc-002: in 100% of automated checks, editing live planned dates afte
nodes.rationale: In 100% of automated checks, editing live planned dates after baseline lock leaves locked baseline snapshot dates unchanged.

nodes.label: SC-003: Approving a schedule change request always yields a new base
nodes.norm_label: sc-003: approving a schedule change request always yields a new base
nodes.rationale: Approving a schedule change request always yields a new baseline version while retaining the previous version in 100% of automated checks.

nodes.label: SC-004: When durations or relations are incomplete, critical-path ou
nodes.norm_label: sc-004: when durations or relations are incomplete, critical-path ou
nodes.rationale: When durations or relations are incomplete, critical-path output is labeled not valid / not calculable in 100% of automated checks (no authoritative false path).

nodes.label: SC-005: The milestone/delay report distinguishes approved, current,
nodes.norm_label: sc-005: the milestone/delay report distinguishes approved, current,
nodes.rationale: The milestone/delay report distinguishes approved, current, actual, and forecast date sets whenever each set has data (verified in acceptance tests).
